item.title: Using Gemini agent teams to optimize quantum algorithms
item.description:
Using Gemini agent teams to optimize quantum algorithms

Researchers have utilized teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms by creating highly efficient quantum circuits. This approach uses proof-checked AI search to compress years of manual design work into efficient instructions for quantum hardware.

🧩 How it works

To ensure the reliability of resource-intensive circuits that cannot be tested on classical computers or current processors, the agent teams used Lean, a formal theorem prover, to mathematically guarantee the results. Researchers directed the agents by specifying problem parameters and supervising their progress to achieve these results.

⚙️ Key details

The agents successfully reduced computational costs and memory requirements for several complex scientific applications and fundamental operations:

Algorithm/Application Improvement Metric
Inertial Confinement Fusion 11.8× Cost
Light-sensitive molecule simulation 8× Cost
Cytochrome P450 2.5× Speedup
Grover’s algorithm 2.57× Speedup
Arcsin routine 290× Speedup

💡 Why it matters

Optimized quantum circuits are essential for running future simulations that address complex scientific challenges. While current improvements do not yet reach the threshold required for the first error-corrected quantum computers, they represent significant progress in areas such as fusion energy, drug design, and photochemical reaction simulations.

🚀 Availability

The team has open-sourced their Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub to encourage community collaboration.

#QuantumComputing #Gemini #AIAgents #Lean #ScientificResearch

Source: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification

item.title: Slurm 26.11 Introduces HRES to Enable Native Quantum Processor Scheduling
item.description:
Slurm 26.11 Introduces HRES to Enable Native Quantum Processor Scheduling

Slurm 26.11 adds Hierarchical Resources (HRES) plugins that enable quantum processing units (QPUs) to be scheduled as native cluster resources, allowing HPC centers to integrate quantum accelerators alongside traditional supercomputing systems.

🔍 Overview

National programs across North America, Europe, and Asia are integrating quantum processing units (QPUs) into supercomputing centers worldwide. These QPUs operate as cluster-wide accelerators, distinct from node-attached GPUs.

🧩 How it works

The HRES plugin interface uses short, portable Lua scripts to manage QPU scheduling:

  • Reports device health to the scheduler
  • Accepts device options as part of resource requests
  • Runs setup and teardown code at each job stage
  • Describes QPUs to HPC software via QRMI and QDMI open source efforts

⚙️ Key details

The architecture differs fundamentally from GPU scheduling:

Feature GRES (GPUs) HRES (QPUs)
Scope Per compute node Cluster-wide
Management Built into Slurm Plugin-based
Access Jobs on specific node Jobs on allowed nodes

A QPU is modeled using a single layer in resources.yaml covering nodes that can reach the device, with a count of one. The plugin logic is separate from site configuration, allowing vendors to distribute it across installations.

🚀 Availability

HRES entered Slurm in version 25.05 as a beta feature and reached production maturity in version 26.11, representing an evolution of the licensing mechanism with similar counting semantics but node-specific associations.

#Slurm #QuantumComputing #HPC #Supercomputing #QPU #Scheduling

Source: Integrating QPUs into Supercomputing Centers Using Slurm HRES Plugins | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: AI system from Physical Superintelligence proves Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum conjecture
item.description:
AI system from Physical Superintelligence proves Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum conjecture

Physical Superintelligence, an AI science startup, announced that its internal AI system produced a proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis quantum computing conjecture.

🔍 Overview

  • The conjecture, formulated by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis, has been open since 2008 and concerns when quantum computers can be exponentially faster than ordinary ones.
  • Physical Superintelligence (PSI) developed a research system that runs a non‑public Anthropic model.
  • During the third day of a run, the system generated a complete proof of the conjecture, which was accepted by the Lean proof assistant.
  • The system was then tasked with related open problems, improving the result twice, with Lean accepting the final version.

🧩 How it works

  • PSI’s internal system leverages an Anthropic language model to explore mathematical reasoning.
  • The model searches for a sequence of logical steps that constitute a proof.
  • Each candidate proof is fed to Lean, which checks every inference mechanically.
  • Acceptance by Lean confirms the proof’s correctness.

⚙️ Key details

Aspect Fact
Conjecture origin Open since 2008, by Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis
Proof discovery time Complete proof appeared on the third day of the run
Verification tool Lean proof assistant accepted the proof
Iterations System improved the result twice, with Lean accepting the final version

💡 Why it matters

“we’re in the early stages of the singularity, defined as the period when the rate of technological and scientific progress exceeds the rate at which we humans can parse out and make sense of it.”

“Research like this is a taste of what that means; mostly automated synthetic researchers extending the frontier of knowledge, spitting out results which need to then be understood by humans.”

These statements highlight the significance of AI‑generated proofs as an example of automated synthetic researchers extending the frontier of knowledge.

#QuantumComputing #AutomatedProofs #AIResearch

Source: Import AI 480: Self-sustaining space economies; AI for science progress, and Meta builds perfect hands for a superintelligence
